rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: So what is this important thing you need to tell me about?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Haha, yeah, that important thing.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Dad, are you hiding something from me?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Ah, I knew I couldn't hide it for long. Himeko...
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: I am sick.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: What?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: This isn't the right place for this discussion. Let's go to my office.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: So...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's the Weathering Curse.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: I know what you're about to ask. I do not share the Graphia lineage, which is why I believed I could find the "demon from beyond" and save you and your mother.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: But in the end, Ryusuke was just a useless man who couldn't save his wife or daughter...
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Or even himself.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Tell me, what happened in the past fifteen years?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You've seen my portfolio, haven't you? Those worlds are just like Planarcadia. Every single one of them has fallen victim to the "demon from beyond."
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: In those places, "luck" is a very real thing, and the Demon From Beyond can manipulate "misfortune."
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: What does that even mean?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In ways beyond comprehension, you feel misfortune crashing down like a tidal wave. Solar storms, diamond rain, system failures, one disaster after another...
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: But if you make it out alive, bizarre strokes of luck come swarming back to you. And so the cycle repeats, washing over the world, tearing it apart.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: It sounds more insane than the Phantasmoon Games.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The universe is sheer madness, beyond all reason. I've survived over and over, yet my body has become as fragmented as Graphia once was.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Is this his way of torturing the rebels? I don't know. But by the time I realized it...
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: There was no escape.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Why didn't you tell me earlier? I could've reached out to the IPC's doctors...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's no use. I've been chasing after him my whole life. I know him better than you do.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Himeko, remember when you first learned to paint? I told you then why we must paint the beauty that we see.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: "Because the ugly, the despicable, and the cowardly, they endure forever through evasion, like beasts driven by survival."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: "Beauty remains ever fleeting, just as heroes find their end in sacrifice and stars dissolve after they shine. Humans have surpassed their animal nature. We face our pain and our end to win a dignity that the vast universe cannot ignore."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: "So we must capture what is noble and bright to show that such things truly lived. As for the barbaric and the low, they will endure regardless, needing no witness to their existence."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But Himeko, you are no longer the one who paints. You have become the very splendor that I strive to capture.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Fate works in mysterious ways. I am so glad to see you once more in my final moments, watching you fulfill your childhood dream. You are standing before me, as the navigator of Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: I should've come back earlier. I'm so sorry.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: No, I am the one who came back too late.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: I've thought about it a thousand times. On that final night of the Bloodstained Games, if only someone had been there to sit by your side...
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: After everything, does this tardy father still even deserve to hear what his daughter wants to say?
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: If you're willing.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I'll tell you about everything that happened.
Thank you, Akivili...
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Thank you, Himeko.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: All of this happened after you went away. You were jumping from one job to the next, and for four long years, I had heard nothing from you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: During those four years, I found the stranded Express deep in the canvas world and kept trying to repair it. Watching the Phantasmoon grow fuller, I remembered the mask that had been handed down through our family for generations.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: If I could claim victory in the Phantasmoon Games, then perhaps, by harnessing the divine authority of Elation, it might just be possible to set the Express in motion once more.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But the Herald of Death was a complete madman, and he smashed every dream to pieces...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Huff... huff...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: These bloodstains... The Herald of Death is heading to Dovebrook.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: He's already killed so many people. When will it be enough!?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Fifteen years ago...
You're asking if I'm afraid?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Of course I am, after seeing all that carnage along the way.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Belle, Meeya... Everyone was splattered everywhere, like spray paint.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Twisted and crushed.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: They watched themselves turn into... while they were still alive...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Mm. I'm okay. I'm fine.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: If I don't stop him right here and win the Phantasmoon Games, there will be no tomorrow for anyone, let alone a new journey for the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: And someone needs to avenge those students at the academy.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I know hunting down the Herald of Death isn't my responsibility. If I turn around and walk away, no one will blame me.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: But I am already here. I can't let him get away.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Yeah, I'm not really scared anymore. Really.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: The suppression squad sent by the Department of Aberration Defense... They're all gone. Completely wiped out.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: They struggled through the pain as the Herald of Death dragged and smeared them across the ground...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: But these stains... Is he really so far gone that he's using himself as "paint"?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Even so, he still managed to break through the blockade ahead... That's terrifying.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I think I've got it.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: But first, I need to buy some time.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Alright, but buying time is easier said than done.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: It's too narrow here. We need more room. The best bet is to pin the Herald down on that bridge.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I'll take all the wishpower I've gathered since the Phantasmoon became full and use it as fuel to paint "it" into existence.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: The sheer destructive force unleashed from creating a massive object will break him and leave him completely incapacitated.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Yeah... By burning all the Wishpower, I will be forfeiting my victory.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: But even if I did win the games and restart the Express... What would happen to this city? To my friends, my teachers, and everyone else? Where would they have left to go?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: To set the Express in motion with Aha's power, while standing by as innocent people are slaughtered by monsters... To soar into the stars, while turning a deaf ear to the screams on the ground.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Someone who does that... has no right to call themselves a Nameless.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Ugh, I knew I should have stuffed an orbital cannon or a molecular saw into the case. Using that bigger-on-the-inside Trailblaze tech, just like the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Right. When this is all over, I will have to give it a try.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Another body...
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Black Birch the Masked Fool... The one who turned Gothum City upside down not long ago!?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Only two Supplicants are left in the Games now.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: Just like those legends I grew up with. A hero confronting a monster to protect everyone. Now that responsibility falls to me.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: I will take him down. After that I will repair the Express myself and see it fly over the horizon and break out of the atmosphere.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: The very first stop then?
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: It'll certainly be quite memorable.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: This stench... It's about time.
rows.speaker: Young Himeko

rows.text: So exquisite! These flowers blooming in Planarcadia. I can hear them, dancing at the tips of my nerves.
rows.speaker: Herald of Death

rows.text: What is that? You say this is not enough?
rows.speaker: Herald of Death

rows.text: Still not enough! I need more pigment. I will mix my colors with screams of terror and pray for the catecholamines to drown me.
rows.speaker: Herald of Death

rows.text: Department Head! I shall show you the error of your ways! This flesh is the culmination of life. Its own kin is right here, the giant tree running through Ahatopia!
rows.speaker: Herald of Death

rows.text: I shall become her. We will be as one. No. I will surpass her. I will devour her and become the one and only existence.
rows.speaker: Herald of Death

rows.text: Another new shade. Dazzling, shattered crimson... Are you perhaps the color I've been missing all along?
rows.speaker: Herald of Death

rows.text: Step into this masterpiece! Become one with me, and lay the final cornerstone for the future of human evolution!
rows.speaker: Herald of Death

rows.text: Stop right there!
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: So you actually conquered the Herald of Death and set the Astral Express in motion once more at the end of the Bloodstained Games?
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Himeko, I believe in your bravery. When confronted by death, you will undoubtedly choose to resist.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: But you were so frail and sickly. How could you possibly defeat the Herald of Death who slaughtered every single Supplicant? And how could you hope to repair such a massive, stranded Express?
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: The answer is clear. It would be impossible for you. That is, unless...
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Unless you had another person helping you.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Don't deny it yet.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: I've been tested by you enough along the way. So now give your father a little room to breathe.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: While I was gathering your belongings, I found some of the manuscripts you left behind. There were two distinct sets of handwriting upon those pages. Every trace in that house proves that two people once shared a life there.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Legend says that during the Canvas Age, the Grand Artist Whitebow painted his late daughter onto a scroll and breathed life into her.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Suppose, just suppose, that my brilliant daughter created a likeness of herself, a self-portrait so perfect that it breathed and moved with her.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: If that is the truth, then every mystery is explained.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: During that night of the Bloodstained Games, a girl at death's door and an imagenae she created followed the trail of the Herald of Death all the way to Dovebrook.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: As a monster bearing Shuhu's Flesh and a Supplicant lost to madness, Marcus Antali defeated the pair before him without lifting a finger.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Driven by pure instinct, he slowly closed in on them. He intended to use their very lives as pigment to paint a new Bloody Bloom.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Little did he know that he was walking straight into a trap of their design.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: The moment he drew near, a massive iron fist was imagenated from the sky above. It crashed down and crushed him to dust.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: It was the night of July 22, 1984 of the Arcadian Calendar. A colossal shockwave, radiating from Dovebrook District, shook the earth. As the dust settled, a strange urban legend found its way into every corner of the world.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Over ten thousand sightings reported a giant arm descending from the sky that evening. In the hours that followed, the Department of Aberration Defense confirmed that the Herald of Death was completely incapacitated.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: The theories were endless. Was it a divine act by Aha, or a weapon built by the IPC? No one knew for sure. Yet, the silhouette of that giant remained etched in every mind as a testament to heroism.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: It was just an arm, yet beneath the brush of a girl who yearned for the stars, it became an extension of humanity's reach.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: The girl achieved her dream, and the stars set sail once more. Truly a most romantic fairy tale. And now...
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Unfortunately, I have to destroy this fairy tale myself.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: You don't believe me?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I have no idea who you truly are. But that little girl who longed for Trailblazing, my frail and sickly daughter...
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: From the very beginning, "Himeko" never left Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: That is not something you should joke about.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You know better than I do whether I'm joking or not.
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: By the way, things outside aren't looking good. The arcadia is drowning in problems. Is it really wise to stay here instead of helping the younger crew members?
rows.speaker: Ryusuke

rows.text: Those kids are all grown up now. They can handle their mission. And as for myself...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I am staying right here, to deal with the biggest problem of all.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Technically, you shouldn't be moving the set pieces here without permission. But in a crisis like this, who cares about a few measly hotel management regulations?
In any case, once you're done borrowing it, you can always play a couple rounds of snowball fights with Casper to make up for it.
Besides us, there are plenty of ancient imagenae living here, ones that've long gone extinct elsewhere. Some even claim to be original works by Graphia herself.
rows.speaker: Grafia

rows.text: If you're serious about finding Graphia, you should try asking them!
rows.speaker: Grafea

rows.text: Would you like to take the ferry to Inkford Hermitage?
rows.speaker: Feld

rows.text: Board the ferry.
Hold on.
Please wait a moment. I'll arrange a shuttle for you right away.
rows.speaker: Feld

rows.text: Understood. Come find me when you need to catch a ferry.
rows.speaker: Feld

rows.text: World in Canvas! Wanna go? Wanna go?
rows.speaker: Wispae

rows.text: Let's go!
Not right now.
Into the canvas! Into the canvas!
rows.speaker: Wispae

rows.text: Casper? Are you there?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Nope... I'm not.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: We have arrived. This is the snowy shore of the canvas world, Inkford Hermitage.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: Are those wispae floating on the water?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Mighty! Wishpower! Mighty! Superstar!
rows.speaker: Wispae

rows.text: Oh dear, there are so many wispae. They are blocking the boat's route.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: But no need to panic. Please follow my lead.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: Is that...?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Ah, the golden tree in the distance? We call it "Myriad Wish Grove."
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: It's said that it shares the same lineage as the sacred trees on the floating island of Seafeld and the Phantasmoon Courtyard.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: Before entering the canvas, the imagenae go there to return their wishes, setting out unburdened.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: Even next to such a lively hot spring hotel, there's a secluded mountain path like this.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: These atonement statues all look like small animals.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I should find a prominent spot for the ground lamps.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You are too kind. I followed the battle in Seafeld City very closely. Serving a hero such as yourself is a true privilege.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: I see. It so happens that Madam Pearl is tied up with an unforeseen event, so allow me to brief you in her stead.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: Well, Graphia's former residence was located there.
Yes. To be precise, she lived there a thousand years ago.
Legend says the miraculous encanvasing of the mortal world happened there. Would Madam Pearl, a die-hard fan, pass up a sacred site like that?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Word is that Madam Pearl just flicked her wrist, signed a check with an astronomical figure, and bought the whole plot of land. She also snatched up every single piece of Graphia's "lost works" she could find, without bothering to verify their authenticity.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: This is the author of Fluffy Across the Blue, Blurry_QR_Colt.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Well yes. Would you believe it if I said I was going on vacation?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: It's only normal for a famous comic artist to travel with bodyguards, no?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Miss Blurry_QR_Colt, let's be clear. You are being transported under escort.
rows.speaker: Bodyguard A

rows.text: Hey, I pay for my own meals. Is that so shocking to you? Is it?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: No way! It's obviously... all Madam Pearl's fault!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I went all-in on Learned Coins... there goes my licensing fees and royalties.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: So you're escorting her to... uh, shall we say, an "intensive creative retreat"?
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: The boat has arrived. When you're ready, let's begin our journey to Inkford Hermitage. Please, mind your step as you board.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: Little ol' me... was once a tall, mighty, and majestic giant. Of course, that was back in the Cindearth Age.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Hehe... indeed, another glittering Nameless.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Sightings of Lady Graphia are as common as the snowflakes here!
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: If she wanted to see her, it would already have happened. The IPC has practically turned the World in Canvas upside down.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: A friend of Graphia's? Just how long has that person been alive...?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Normally, I'd suggest you play that little snow puffball for info. That "good luck with your inquiries" line definitely had a subtext.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Oh right, that was your big adventure in Penacony! How nice. I hope Planarcadia holds one too.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Hahaha... I was just kidding.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Hahaha... I was just kidding.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: S—Sorry... I was just trying to lift the mood.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I don't care which, one of you, come help me fight a Lord Ravager.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: If you're looking for the real Graphia, I'd suggest you give up.
rows.speaker: Grafia

rows.text: Who knows? Maybe the IPC made up some story to boost the hotel's revenue.
rows.speaker: Graphea

rows.text: There's one very simple way!
rows.speaker: Grafea

rows.text: As I suspected, finding Graphia was never going to be easy.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Yes. This old soul is just scraping by with what little talent I have left.
rows.speaker: Fatigued Kappa

rows.text: To think there are still those who recognize my kind. You are quite well-informed.
rows.speaker: Fatigued Kappa

rows.text: The humans here call me "Sudscour," filthy name, but fitting for this frail and wretched form.
rows.speaker: Sudscour

rows.text: As you see. My kin have either been swallowed by the muddy currents or have fled into the canvas.
rows.speaker: Sudscour

rows.text: It is hard to leave one's homeland. Even when my kin have entered the canvas, even when the waters here are no longer clear, and even when the new Ploo tribe has replaced us...
rows.speaker: Sudscour

rows.text: Upon hearing that name, the withered body of Ahatopia's last kappa begins to tremble faintly.
Legend says that when she was a painter, she was a woman of radiant beauty.
rows.speaker: Sudscour

rows.text: As long as the World in Canvas exists, Lady Graphia must as well.
rows.speaker: Sudscour

rows.text: If you seek clues regarding Lady Graphia, you should visit the mountain behind the hotel.
rows.speaker: Sudscour

rows.text: That is all I can tell you. After all, I am just a stubborn old kappa trying to keep this one pool of water a little cleaner.
rows.speaker: Sudscour

rows.text: A snowball... fight? Ah, the game... the name... it feels so familiar.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: She was a great painter who led us in snowball fights! She'd even paint portraits for everyone!
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: There was someone else. Just thinking about them makes my blood boil...
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: I saw her once... just once.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: I only shared some memories of a snowball fight. If it helped you, Nameless, then I'm happy.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Why are you saying that too? It's making me feel all strange.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: That's about all Casper can remember. If you're still up for fun and games, come find me for another snowball fight sometime!
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Who dares disturb my thousand-year slumber...
Thanks for the invite. I'm not quite dead yet, but I don't feel alive either.
I'm... I'm testing the deadline. I snuck out.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I was hoping to find some inspiration out here! With those two goons breathing down my neck, anyone would hit a complete creative block.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Give me a break! I REALLY am just looking for inspiration out here!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Look at this old stone statue. Doesn't it look like Himekat?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Hmm? You're asking me? Weren't you the one searching so desperately for me?
Child, you were the one who lit the ground lamps, were you not? If memory serves, that was the secret signal my old friends used to call for me.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Since Ahatopia's encanvasing, Evanescia and I agreed to guard reality and the World in Canvas separately, never to meet again.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: My, you certainly have a lot of questions. But before I enlighten you...
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Hmm, I see you're carrying something that might be proof enough...
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: She painted a Supplicant's Mask for you?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: The red-haired girl reaches out and takes the mask.
Hmph. Such crude brushwork... there's no doubt that this is her handiwork.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Indeed. That tower, which stood only for a moment, was the crashed Astral Express. And Graphia's family name, "Murata," came from the wondrous sight she saw.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: She lost. Graphia did not win the Phantasmoon Games, nor did she manage to kill Asat Pramad.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Yes. As long as "the scroll" still enshrouds reality, he won't be able to lay a finger on the leviathan's remains buried deep within Ahatopia.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: So, are we leaving right now?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: They probably sensed your Wishpower. You are the Phantasmoon Games superstar, no?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Must've been when we came ashore, what a devoted fan.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} [Trailblazer], it is an honor to... well, shall I say, be of service to you again?
rows.speaker: Reception Staff

rows.text: To be honest, when Madam Pearl invited you to visit the Pearluxe Tower, I was supposed to be your guide. I ended up being replaced by a total fraud.
rows.speaker: Reception Staff

rows.text: My name is Feld. By order of Madam Pearl, I will be escorting you to your destination.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: Thank you, Mr. Feld.
I assume Madam Pearl has already briefed you on our destination?
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: No.
The destination of our boat journey is a hotel known as "Inkford Hermitage."
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: It is situated at the end of a Dovebrook tributary that ultimately flows into the sea. It is one of the points where the World in Canvas intersects with reality.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: What does this have to do with Graphia?
Graphia lived there?
Nihilux! When did you get here?
Whew... I guess money really does let you do whatever you want.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That's not even the half of it. I don't know where her obsession comes from, but she's dead set on the idea that Graphia is still alive. If she gets even a whiff of anything remotely related to Graphia, she's got her people on it at the snap of a finger.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: But all they could find were imagenae knock-offs: random, pretty red-heads based on nothing but imagination.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I bet her reaction went something like this: "Objective: Locate the original. Error: Detecting excessive quantity of low-quality merchandise."
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You! I remember you! You're that fraudster from Pearluxe Tower!
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: Pearluxe Tower!? I've never set foot in that place in my life!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Oh, I know it's you! I've seen the footage. You're wearing the exact same outfit!
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: Argh... A slip-up in an otherwise perfect plan! Relax, your job is safe this time.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Cut it out, you scoundrel! You can't talk your way out of this! Who exactly are you?
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: Huh... Hmm... Is that so.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: My apologies, how rude of me. Miss Colt, it's an honor to finally see the face behind the work. Please pardon my yelling. I didn't know.
rows.speaker: Agent Feld

rows.text: Hehe, no worries, no worries.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Are you headed to Inkford Hermitage as well?
Who are those two big fellas behind you?
Your current credit balance is in the negative. Madam Pearl has offered you a lifeline by asking you to complete the next volume of The Fluffy.
rows.speaker: Bodyguard B

rows.text: Whoa, this is not my fault. Remember Alloy King Pom-Pom from Pearluxe Tower? I tried to put everything on Pearl's tab, but she found out and charged it back to me.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Who knew a figurine could be so expensive? It cost me more than my entire savings.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You actually have savings?
Oh right, so, it's mine then?
Didn't you just release a new volume? How are you still broke?
I lost every single penny!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Correct. The objective is to deliver the manuscript and clear her debts. The estimated duration is 56 days.
rows.speaker: Bodyguard B

rows.text: Hear that, [Trailblazer]? It's not a hotel. It's hell! Where you get whipped for not finishing your scripts on time!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Good luck with that.
Ugh, you found me, current Nameless. I knew you'd come ask about Lady Graphia.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: But if I try too hard to remember things from such a long, long time ago, my soft, squishy head starts to throb... and then I start melting: drip-drop, drip-drop.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: So much of my memory feels like it's shrouded in a blizzard, and I can't see anything clearly... I'm sorry, but I don't think I can help you.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: I'm just here for a snowball fight.
It feels like I had snow ball fights every single day, a long time ago. Shaping the snow into balls and, hehe, flinging them at whatever strange intruders came barging in.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Well then, come at me, Nameless! I'm a snowball fight veteran, I won't lose.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Phew... things from the Cindearth Age are still a bit blurry.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: But I definitely met Lady Graphia! I had snowball fights with her!
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: What was she like?
Back then, when we wanted to see her, we'd go to her doorstep, light the ground lamps, and shout "snowball fight!"
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Then Lady Graphia would poke her head out the window upstairs, unfurl a scroll, and whoosh—slide right down onto the snow.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Then we'd have snowball fights against the Voidrangers together, under the giant moon.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: If we won, I got to swallow the Voidrangers whole. Mmm, they were so crispy and tasty.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Can you remember anything else?
He was a snowball fight master. I remember one time, eight of us teamed up to challenge him.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: But that guy knocked us all down with his snowballs like it was nothing, all from so far away!
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Six of my friends were lying on the ground, feeling beat. Losing the game got everyone so down that no one uttered a word.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: As for me, I think I got hit right in the neck. I saw my own giant body thud onto the ground, and my chin felt ice-cold.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: (Eight people... in the Phantasmoon Games? Perhaps "snowball fight" is a euphemism for the Cindearth Age wars...?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (So in that round of the Phantasmoon Games, Graphia must have fought a terrifyingly powerful opponent. It seems only she and Casper survived the fight.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Have you seen Graphia since?
By then, Ahatopia had already been transported into the canvas. It was so quiet and lonely.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: I couldn't find my other six friends, but I remembered where Lady Graphia lived.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: So I went to her front door again, lit the ground lamps, and shouted: "Snowball fight!"
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: It felt like only a second had passed, just the blink of an eye, yet somehow it also felt like forever. At last, I saw her drift out.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: She held me and cried, saying "I'm sorry" and "you've done well" over and over...
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Hmm, it was just one lost game. We could have just won it back some other time. But... that was the last I saw of her.
rows.speaker: Casper

rows.text: Thank you, Casper.
You've done well all these years.
(So, to summarize, Casper likes to light the ground lamps and call for her near Graphia's old home.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Now, where can I find those ground lamps?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: These two little lamps... don't look reliable at all...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Whatever, it's not like I have any other way.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Show yourself, Lady Graphia!
Not only will I refuse to grant you three wishes, I shall also lock you in my canvas to suffer in my stead!
Ahh! Are you dead or alive?
You again, Colt!
This mountain path is so quiet and secluded. What a great spot for a night stroll. Listening to the calming sound of the springs, who knows? Maybe my inspiration will flow again like these waters.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Your inspiration is dry, but your excuses for missing deadlines certainly aren't.
I'm going to shout!
I just reached the "Real vs. Fake Himekat" arc in my comic. Let me pay my respects. Maybe Graphia will bless me with enlightenment.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Miss Colt, when did you sneak out?
That was fast!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I let my guard down for just one second, and corporate asset — I mean Miss Colt — escaped. Now that's scary.
rows.speaker: Bodyguard A

rows.text: No way are you running away and taking our jobs with you. Good thing this kind lady spotted where you were headed, otherwise, you might've slipped away for real.
rows.speaker: Bodyguard B

rows.text: Let's go. Back to the room to finish your work.
rows.speaker: Bodyguard A

rows.text: Come on, not again! [Trailblazer]! Help...!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Nihilux is hauled away by two bodyguards, leaving only her drawn-out cries for help echoing across the hillside.
Whew. Being an artist sure is grueling. I remember being held in a room and watched by six or seven people, too. I wasn't allowed to leave until I finished painting either.
Why are you still here?
My name is Murata Graphia, Guardian of the World in Canvas. It is a pleasure to meet you, Nameless of the Astral Express.
You're saying... you are Graphia?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (She really does look a lot like Himeko.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Can you prove who you say you are?
I simply answered the call, yet you doubt my identity. How strange.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Let me think... I believe I know why you've come to find me.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: The {RUBY_B#Evanescia}arbitrator of the Phantasmoon Games{RUBY_E#} asked you to tell me that our old enemy, the Demon Lord From Beyond, has returned. Am I correct?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: You know about that?
But over the past thousand years, I often hoped we might reunite in some way.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Who would've thought, when word of her finally reached me again, there'd be no warm greetings, but instead only an impending crisis.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: [Trailblazer], you must have many questions.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: During the Cindearth Age, that Demon Lord From Beyond once took the form of a friend to infiltrate the resistance, causing catastrophic casualties. I must confirm your identity, Nameless.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Do you carry a token from Evanescia?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: A token? I don't remember having anything like that.
If you mean something Evanescia gave me, there's only this.
Hey, give it back. It's very important.
The red-haired girl hands the mask back to you.
The secrets you seek are many and tangled. Perhaps I should start by telling you a story.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: A thousand years ago, the Legions of the Demons From Beyond descended upon Ahatopia, marking the beginning of the Cindearth Age.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: For the Destruction, taking a life is easier than brushing aside a feather. Among the countless victims, a baby girl was saved by a painter from the brink of death. He took her in as his daughter and named her Graphia.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: To protect his daughter, the painter kept her confined to their home. While the fires of disaster swept across the land, Graphia lived in seclusion.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Until one day, a falling star streaked across the dark sky, and a deafening roar shattered the silence of the wasteland.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Unable to contain her curiosity, the young girl slipped out of the house to follow the sound.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: And so she saw it: beneath the cold Phantasmoon, a "Tower of Infinity" stood on the mountain range at the edge of the horizon.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: This "tower" had countless windows and rose section by section, slender and tall. More than an actual tower, it looked like a wounded iron dragon that had fallen to the earth.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Is that the origin of the "Murata" name?

At the time, the wrecked train was surrounded by countless abominable monsters. Amidst these foul enemies, a few warriors in strange attire fought tirelessly, but they fell one by one, unable to withstand the endless tide of monsters.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: It was only much later that Graphia understood that those who fought and died for Ahatopia shared a common name...
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: The Nameless, who walk the path of the Trailblaze.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: That was the day that Graphia stepped into the mortal world. Her life as the Mother of Imagenesis began.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: In a long, drawn-out war fought at a severe disadvantage, she was forced to seek the aid of the Phantasmoon Games, attempting to use the mighty power of an Aeonic ritual to lock the terrifying Demon Lord From Beyond within a limited battlefield.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: This was also the first time in the history of the Phantasmoon Games that the eight Supplicants joined forces to confront a powerful enemy from beyond: the Lord Ravager, Asat Pramad.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Did she win?
In the final days of the Cindearth Age, she gathered every ounce of Wishpower to paint the world into a scroll. Using herself as a nail to steady the canvas, she sealed the Lord Ravager outside.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: She made a seal capable of shutting out a Lord Ravager?
The story is over. I have received Evanescia's message.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: I also have a token I'd like you to give her. Please, let us journey together to the other side.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: No, there is no need to rush. You have a friend here who is lingering with a heart full of farewells.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: You mean... Blade?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Follow this path down to the riverbank of Myriad Wish Grove. You'll find many wispae gathered there.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: When you are ready, choose a wispae. Whisper Graphia's name and your wish to cross over to the other shore, then release the wispae into the river.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: When the time comes, I will bring the ferry to deliver you into the canvas.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: (Graphia vanished? How elusive.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Anyway, I should head to the riverbank of Myriad Wish Grove first.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...You are unusually talkative today. Are you trying to buy time?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: ...Then I shall begin with that lone island of Insumousu.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: It was a desolate wasteland, untouched and forgotten. Desolate, cold. The perfect place to lay the dead to rest.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: I planted rusted, broken blades in the wasteland as a mark of my departure. Little did I know that even after joining the Stellaron Hunters, I would find myself returning there time and again, bringing along a few new swords with me.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Their owners, some of them sought my life, only to fall by my hand. Others simply wished to see me one last time as their own lives flickered out.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: I was once a craftsman. And those swords... They were all my own creations.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: I raised those wordless monuments for my old friends, one by one, until they became a forest of broken blades.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: And what about... me?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: And my sword... When will it finally join them in that forest?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: He finally smiled, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I'm actually the one who can't even smile. This sucks...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: (sigh)...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Next time, it'd be better if you didn't try to sneak up on us like that.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: We've been here for a while. If you'd come any later, you'd be looking for him inside the belly of Voracity.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I get it. It was a deliberate "accident."
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I knew you would come.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: I met the legendary Graphia. She told me a way to enter the World in Canvas.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I will keep the secret.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: You talk too much.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: You talk too much.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: ...Thank you.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Before you go, you have something to say to [Trailblazer] too, right?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: We use the script to interfere with the future.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Then, let it be.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: (Graphia vanished? How elusive.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Anyway, I should head to the riverbank of Myriad Wish Grove first.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I've heard that in the same forest, giant trees will fight each other for nutrients...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: How about this: we just feed Shuhu to that tree in the Courtyard. It would save us a long trip.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Say something.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Didn't know you were a forestry expert.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: I'm not joking. I'm serious.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: If the Elwood absorbed another Emanator of Abundance, it would likely bring about an even greater catastrophe.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Right now, there is no other option besides the Voracity husk.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: If the Abundance grows too strong, the Ambrosial Arbor loses control, and the arcadia is doomed. If the Abundance is too weak, the husk spirals out of control, and the arcadia is doomed just the same...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: It's called an "arcadia", but the whole thing is built on a razor's edge. Does that mean the essence of the Elation is just dark humor?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: You're afraid.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: I'm not. I respect your choice.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Aaarghh, fine! You're right! I'm afraid! So what?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: You think I don't know what that Xianzhou person meant? "One-in-ten chance"? There is no chance at all!
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Listen — I just can't stand by and watch one of my kin sacrifice himself.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Kin...
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: What else? Friend? Colleague? Playmate? The guy who carries my bags when we go shopping?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I suppose all of those fit.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Fit how!?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Sometimes, I can't tell if you're actually dumb or just playing dumb...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I hear you. Just assume it's the former. Simpler that way.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: My mind is made up. You should understand: misplaced emotions will only cause the mission to fail.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: You really are just playing dumb.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Ugh... To be honest, I'm the same way.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: If I could see Firefly cured of her illness, Kafka finally finding the "heart" she's looking for, and [Trailblazer] reclaiming {M#his}{F#her} future...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Then I'd be willing to pick up that "LV.999" cartridge too, even if... it means becoming nothing but a shadow of the Dark Zone.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Don't. At the TV Tower, you already severely overspent your time. Don't touch that thing again.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Besides, why are you telling me this? You should tell them yourself.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Because just like you... I'm a total! Stuck-up! Softie! Happy now?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Feel better?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: No. Unless you give me a sincere apology and a proper goodbye, we're not settled.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Not settled... is that right?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Fair enough.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: (Whether as "Yingxing" or as "Blade," my journey has reached its end.)
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: (Before the final verdict...)
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: (I should say a proper goodbye to my "kin.")
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: ...Who's there?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Hold your fire, it's me.
When did you get here?
Sorry, didn't mean to eavesdrop.
If we simply chant her name and release a wispae into the river, she'll come to ferry us.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: A legend from a thousand years ago... And she's actually still alive?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: It really makes sense. After all, you two are practically the same age. Knowing that gives me a bit more hope that you can actually make it back.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Then let's begin.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Graphia, Graphia! Everyone, into the World in Canvas!
rows.speaker: Wispae

rows.text: How odd. This time, the visitors actually know of my existence?
(Strange... Why is the boat coming from downstream?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I heard your call and have come by boat to guide you across.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Greetings, travelers who seek to leave the mortal world behind. It is a pleasure to meet you.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Oh? Not an imagenae? But someone here to settle the past, and... family members seeing them off?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: I guess so.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: ...The power of Abundance. What a nostalgic scent. There is something terrifying slumbering within you.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: I've heard that something lies at the end of the World in Canvas with the power to suppress it. Will you show us the way?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: I see. You are better informed than I thought.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: I understand. Time is of the essence. Please, step aboard.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Thank you.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: The mountains lie distant, the waters still... and snow settles.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: A fine moment to bring this weary life to its end.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Bring a weary life to its end? To my eyes, the power taking root within you is far from withering away.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: It's just a matter of time.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: The journey downstream is long. As is custom, I must collect your past stories as fare. I shall use them to paint the path forward, which will guide us to the other side.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: My past stories...
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: I am not much of a storyteller.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: There is no need to weave your thoughts into a complete story. A single memory, a single breath... These too are parts of your past.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Only by letting go of the past can you truly set forth with an open heart. Is that not so?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Go ahead, say something. I'm curious too.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: What is this place?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: This is the World in Canvas, a mirror to your soul, blooming as your heart dictates. May this meadow be everything you wished for.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Superb artistry...
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: And yet, I thought you would paint the desolation within me instead.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Desolation?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: I saw no desolation in your story. Instead, I found the lingering regrets of a master craftsman.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: The fire that tempers black steel and shapes a hundred blades does not burn upon the forge or anvil. It burns within your heart.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: That spark within you has yet to fade. It is why this plain has chosen to bloom into flowers.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: We've got no clue what you two are on about with all this cryptic talk...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: But you smiled just now, didn't you?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: ...No, I didn't. We should go.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: We have reached the end.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: That Blue Maw... So, this is it?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Correct. Driven by the buried secrets of Ahatopia, you have come seeking liberation. And now, I have shown you the silhouette of the beast's maw.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: If you should find a way to get out, I ask that you swear to keep this secret.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: That Blue Maw... Can it truly consume the Abundance?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Only a beast of insatiable hunger can end a plague of eternal growth.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: I have stood watch in this realm for a millennium, beholding the eternal conflict where the Voracity and the Abundance remain locked in strife.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: O undying soul... The fate that awaits within those depths lies far beyond the reach of our conjecture.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Perhaps you will vanish into nothingness in a mere heartbeat, or perhaps, you will endure a millennium of gnawing, constantly regenerating only to suffer once more, with liberation remaining an elusive dream.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Beneath that calm of yours, I can feel an "old friend" lingering: agony.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: This is the price I must bear for becoming one with the "Canvas".
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: You're telling me if he leaps, he has to stay down there and be torn apart for ages?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I'm not okay with this! Yao Guang never said anything about this when we went over the plan!
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I have lived for nearly a millennium. I stopped wishing for a swift end a long time ago.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: If the leviathan does not consume me utterly, then I am still alive. And until that moment comes, I will pin Shuhu to the anvil and swing my hammer, once, twice, and again and again.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: ...Is there really no other way!?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Silver Wolf, I was never one for sentiment. I'll say only this.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: In my past life as a smith, I made it a point to forge something for those friends I found tolerable.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: But ever since I joined the Stellaron Hunters...
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Alright, I get it! You want me to go back and take apart that box Kafka uses as a footrest, right?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: ...You already took it apart?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: A long time ago.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Quite a few treasures in there: a master-crafted blade, a game controller, and a... uh, portable reactor?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: ...That's the armor core reforged from the remains of the Glamoth Queen.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Oh, and a cat scratching post.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: When did you find out about these items?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: "You"? You mean "We". We all found out.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Think you hid it that well? Please, give me a break. We're a pro team, you know.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Just split it among yourselves. Consider it a keepsake.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Kafka should be the one saying this, but...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: You are the most perfect blade the Stellaron Hunters could ever have.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: ...Just a broken blade, that is all.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: ...To me?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Don't take offense, it's just a few words.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Before joining the Stellaron Hunters, I once lost myself.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Unable to see the future, yet unable to reclaim the past... Just like you when you were first reborn.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Whether we chose this path or were forced onto it...
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: [Trailblazer], leave no room for regret, and never deny the path you've traveled.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: But some things, once spoken aloud before their time arrives, will never come to pass.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: So... I must head into this unscripted path alone. To witness that final, solitary truth for myself.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: It's time.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Do you still remember that passphrase?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: (Two pair...)

rows.text: (Ace... Go.)

rows.text: It might take forever for him to return. Or he might never come back at all.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Or maybe if I just complain and say, "I wish Blade were here," he'll just show up.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Anyway, it was his choice. We already said our goodbyes.

rows.text: No, no, we're far more than just archnemeses...
rows.speaker: Asat Pramad

rows.text: Thank you. For staying with him until the very end.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I will do everything I can to help you...
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Now, it is time to deal with your matters.

Didn't you ask me to come here?
Already told me?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: I don't quite follow.

rows.text: Our first meeting was just before we took the boat here.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: I only answered the call of Wishpower because of that mask, the one painted by Evanescia. Without it, I would not be here.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: So, who is this "me" you speak of?
